definition: Dental phobia is a strong fear related to dental stimuli that can develop through aversive associative learning of dental fear. In this context, prior nonthreatening exposure to dental-related cues may interfere with that learning and reduce the likelihood that dental phobia develops.

reasons: The definition states “a strong fear,” but the packet does not characterize dental phobia/fear as “strong.”

The definition says “prior nonthreatening exposure to dental-related cues may interfere… and reduce the likelihood that dental phobia develops,” but the packet only describes latent inhibition as pre-exposure impairing learning of dental fear from aversive associative conditioning; it does not explicitly describe the pre-exposure as “nonthreatening” or “dental-related cues” in those exact terms.
The packet supports latent inhibition reducing the development of dental fear/dental phobia, but it does not directly define dental phobia as a "strong fear related to dental stimuli."
The phrase "through aversive associative learning" is supported, but the definition adds a broader definitional claim about the nature of dental phobia that is not established in the packet.
